text:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty alert: sustained 502/503 spike on /v1/generate (hosted-api, us-west-2). 18% error rate over 5m. Suspect: encoder-service canary deployment. @maria @eng-oncall please triage

maria: picking this up. checking canary pods now

maria: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=encoder,stack=canary -o wide` -> 3/3 CrashLoopBackOff, restarts 6-12 each

josh: any recent manifest changes?

maria: yes - encoder:v1.3.0 pushed ~1785554000. liveness probe path changed to /livecheck and initialDelaySeconds=5

tim: looking at pod logs: `fatal: failed to load model shards: permission denied` then SIGKILL from kubelet liveness check

maria: copy of pod log: ```2026-06-15T12:24:01 encoder init: extracting shards to /model-cache
2026-06-15T12:24:03 encoder: chmod failed: operation not permitted
2026-06-15T12:24:04 liveness check failed -> killing container```

kate: HPA sighting: hpa/encoder-canary minReplicas=0 targetCPU=10% current replicas ~~auto~~ 0->3 churning. minReplicas=0 is intended for stable but bad for canaries

carla: customers reporting increased 502s for hosted-api; CS queue rising. No broad data loss but some timeouts on regenerations 

maria: I think liveness probe too aggressive + init container permission change -> containers never reach Ready, kubelet kills them before model load. With HPA minReplicas=0 and node drain happening in us-west maintenance, capacity hit and traffic split sent to canary due to rollout config -> increased 502s

josh: can we flip feature flag to cut traffic to canary? Flag: `encoder_rollout_canary` in ff-service

maria: flipping flag now -> `curl -XPOST https://ff.internal/flags/encoder_rollout_canary -d '{"state":"off"}'`

incidents-bot: Feature flag change recorded by audit: encoder_rollout_canary -> off (maria)

carla: thanks, seeing immediate drop in customer errors (some 502s still trickle while backends drain)

maria: rolling back deployment to image encoder:v1.2.9 -> `kubectl rollout undo deploy/encoder -n inference --to-revision=3`

maria: patching liveness probe on canary template: set `initialDelaySeconds: 60`, and remove probe path change -> applying patch now

maria: scaling deployment to stable replicas=4 while HPA root cause investigated: `kubectl scale deploy/encoder --replicas=4 -n inference`

incidents-bot: Rollback started. Notifying oncall-runbook-bot for next steps

oncall-runbook-bot: Runbook check: if canary crashloops + customer 5xx -> rollback + cut traffic + increase probe initialDelay, verify model perms. Escalate to infra if kernel/mount perms involved

josh: checking node drain events - `kubectl get events --field-selector reason=Evicted -n inference` shows mass evictions at 1785554100 from gc-maintenance on three nodes. That decreased capacity during rollout window

tim: investigating permission error: new image changed user from `root` -> `appuser` but init-container still writes as root, emptyDir mount had defaultMode 0755; when pod scheduled on kernels with fs.protected_symlinks it blocks the chmod. We'll need fix in image and manifest

maria: post-rollback health checks passing. `curl https://hosted-api.us-west-2/v1/generate` sample requests now 200, p95 latency back to normal.

carla: CS confirms customer-facing errors resolved, will send update to affected customers that we rolled back a canary and mitigated the issue

kate: action items: 1) revert image changes in canary until perms fix 2) set HPA minReplicas>=1 for canaries or use rollout controller to prevent traffic routing when pods not ready 3) add runbook note about feature-flag quick-cut 4) schedule infra follow-up for mount permission variance across nodes

maria: creating incident ticket and postmortem stub now. I'll include logs, k8s events, and exact commands used. tagging eng-runtime and infra teams

incidents-bot: Incident severity: Sev2 -> mitigated. Root cause: aggressive liveness + image permission changes + simultaneous node maintenance -> insufficient capacity during canary rollout -> increased 502s.

maria: handoff to night oncall at 1785554700. marking incident as under monitoring for 1h.

josh: thanks everyone, reaching out to infra to coordinate image fix and a safer canary gating for next rollout

carla: sending customer notification draft to #customer-updates for review

maria: closing slack thread but leaving incident ticket open for postmortem updates and RCA artifacts.
